pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: When you load a web page, who is the client and who is the server? What defines each role?
expected_points: the browser is the client, the program hosting the site is the server
the client asks first, the server waits for requests and answers
a server is a program in a role, not special hardware

questions.prompt: What does DNS do, and why can't your computer just use example.com directly?
expected_points: DNS resolves human-readable names to IP addresses
packets are delivered to numeric IP addresses, so the name must be translated first
names stay stable while the underlying addresses can change or be several

questions.prompt: Sketch an HTTP exchange for me: what goes in the request, and what comes back in the response?
expected_points: request: a method (GET/POST), a URL/path, headers, optional body
response: a status code, headers, and a body with the content
status code first digit is the category: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error

questions.prompt: Walk me through what happens between typing example.com and seeing the page, step by step.
expected_points: browser completes the URL, then resolves the name via DNS to an IP
opens a connection to that IP on a port, then sends an HTTP GET request
server program builds and sends the response with status, headers, HTML body
browser renders the HTML and issues further requests for referenced resources

questions.prompt: You curl a URL and get a 404. Your friend says the server must be down. Are they right?
expected_points: no — the server answered, so it is up and reachable
4xx means the request was the problem (that path does not exist)
a down server gives no HTTP response at all; a 5xx means the server failed while handling the request

questions.prompt: Is git push 'using the web'? What is the difference between the internet and the web?
expected_points: the internet is the network that moves packets between computers
the web (HTTP in browsers) is one conversation style on top of it
git push is a client/server exchange over the internet too, with git as the client and GitHub as the server
